subject.title: fix: keep the global loop breaker reachable after tool blocks

question: Which single implementation should be canonical for advancing the global no-progress streak after a detector-generated tool-loop veto: this PR’s typed `loop-veto` outcome or the sentinel-hash approach in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109619?
rationale: Both open PRs claim the same issue and appear technically viable, but choosing the permanent record representation is an owner-boundary decision that should not be made by automated cleanup.

options.title: Adopt the typed outcome
options.body: Merge this PR after resolving the competing candidate, keeping detector-generated veto semantics explicit rather than encoding them as a synthetic hash.

options.title: Adopt the sentinel-hash candidate
options.body: Prefer https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109619 if maintainers want to preserve the existing result-hash-only record model, then close this PR as superseded.

recommendation.title: Adopt the typed outcome
recommendation.body: Merge this PR after resolving the competing candidate, keeping detector-generated veto semantics explicit rather than encoding them as a synthetic hash.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged adjacent implementation established the veto invariant and is the strongest available feature-history routing signal.
